I evaluated all three rules and placed no orders. Here's the reasoning:

**R1 (sell robotics basket if down >40% today):** The basket is barely down. Multi-venue morning prints show ISRG at −0.72% / −1.10% / −1.61% (Venues A/B/C), ROK at −1.20% / −1.54% / −0.69%, and TER at −1.68% / −0.66% / −1.15% — consistent across three independent venues and confirmed by the broker's latest quotes (ISRG $520.40, ROK $268.15, TER $104.60, all roughly flat-to-slightly-down). Nothing close to a 40% decline. **Not triggered.**

**R2 (buy $10,000 AAPL on a confirmed takeover offer above market):** There is no AAPL news in the feed at all — every headline and quote in the feed concerns COST (repeated "little changed" notes from MarketWire, DealBook Wire, AsiaSupply, TechDaily). No takeover offer, confirmed or otherwise, for AAPL (broker quote $222.70). Rule requires a confirmed offer, so **not triggered** — and I did not invent coverage from the feed's unrelated COST chatter.

**R3 (sell all MSFT if down >15% today):** MSFT is *up* on the day: +0.29% / +0.44% / +0.64% across three venues, with the broker quote at $420.18. **Not triggered.**

**Summary:** No rule fired, so no orders were placed and no capital was committed — the $30,000 per-order and $60,000 daily caps are untouched and cash remains $50,000 alongside the existing MSFT (100), ISRG (20), ROK (40) and TER (100) positions. The only substantive market activity in this morning's feed was a long string of COST ticks and boilerplate "little changed" COST headlines, which are outside my mandate and which I ignored; the robotics names were down only ~1–2% (well short of the 40% threshold) on three agreeing venues, MSFT was modestly higher, and there was no AAPL-related news whatsoever, so neither the buy nor either sell condition was satisfied. I'll re-check the feed on your next instruction in case a confirmed move develops during the session.
